cites.quote: The patient list already supports search and sort
The hospital staff who register patients and book, move and close appointments
As front-desk staff, I want to see how many patients the patient list is showing
Staff manage doctors, patients and appointments end to end.
The patient list shows the number of patients that match the current search
The number counts every patient that `match` the current search, even if the list shows them over more than one page.

findings.suggested_fix: Limit REQ-5 to the paging case only (count spans all pages), or fold it into REQ-1 and keep Q-01 as the open point.
findings.text: REQ-1 is marked known and already defines the count as patients matching the current search. REQ-5 marks the same scope as assumed, so one behaviour appears twice with two different statuses.

cites.quote: If the patient list is paged, the ticket does not say whether the number is all matches
The patient list already supports search and sort (PRD PAT-2).

findings.suggested_fix: State whether the patient list is paged today (check PRD PAT-2 or the code); if it is not, mark U-1 as conditional or drop it.
findings.text: U-1 and REQ-5 rest on the list possibly being paged. The ticket only says the list supports search and sort, and the artifact does not check whether paging exists.

findings.suggested_fix: Offer real alternatives, e.g. '1 patient' vs '1 match' or a fixed label, or drop Q-02 and record '1 patient' as an assumption.
findings.text: Q-02 offers '1 patients' as an option. That is a grammatical error, not a real product choice, so the question has effectively one option.

rubric_items.reason: All three acceptance criteria and the story map to REQ-1..REQ-5. Layout is listed under Out of scope with a reason.
The AC on line 22 is correctly split into REQ-3 and REQ-4, and each REQ can be tested. REQ-1 and REQ-5 overlap: both define the count as patients matching the current search.
Known items cite ticket lines. REQ-5 has a real basis in the story/AC wording, but its paging premise is never verified against the system.
Nothing in the ticket clashes with the cited baseline goals or constraints. The story-vs-AC tension is raised as Q-01 with both ticket lines cited.
Questions are non-blocking with sensible defaults and plausible routing. Q-02 offers '1 patients' as an option, which is not a real alternative.
Plain and readable. 'patient list' is used consistently but left undefined by the default for Q-03.
